scope: Reduce repeated admitted-overlay serialization and isolate automatic naming discovery SQL

environment.provider: Synthetic naming completion; no external accounts or running user chats

serialization.baseline: New guards fail: one real changed-state browser snapshot encodes the same rows/notices eight times; five repeated/scoped queries encode them five times.
serialization.candidate: Each unchanged admitted overlay encodes once, while same-revision mutations, native fences, read receipts and independent frozen readers remain current.

automaticNaming.mechanism: Existing 32-candidate count/order/window query moves from the event loop to the bounded read-only query process. Host keeps all eligibility, naming and receipt authority.
proofs: 37-candidate canonical query equals the 32-row worker page, including wrap-around
No candidate query executes on the host directory and no dormant session is admitted
Held child permits foreground lock acquisition and ten event-loop scheduling turns
Changed app, native and closed-host facts reject the pending page
Uncommitted state never spawns or exports a query
Canceled read closes its owned child and pending tasks
Timeout and worker early-exit both defer naming and remove the exact child/spool
Existing naming eligibility, cadence, manual-name precedence and persistent attempt suppression pass

limits: Durations are correctness-run elapsed times under other DTU test load, not performance comparisons.
No new quiet 1/6/12-worker timing trial has been run. Prior warm-send and workspace-page target misses remain open.
The earlier sampling profile identifies synchronous naming SQL as remaining main-thread work, but does not prove it accounts for every intermittent workspace delay.
The naming worker still scans indexed catalog metadata; this change isolates that work rather than eliminating it.
Real provider latency, source module preparation, and complete copied-event fidelity are outside these focused proofs.
No spark-1 mutation, release or main merge.
